initial_behavior.baseline: The existing unstable assembly interface closely exposes backend syntax and lacks a user-facing interface suitable for eventual stabilization.
initial_behavior.requested: Define a new assembly macro grammar with explicit operand direction, allocation constraints, output transfer, template substitution, clobbers and optimization flags.

scope_rationale: An independently usable language interface with a full input/operand/behavior/output and compile-time error contract.

mandatory_conditions.predicate: Expose an unsafe assembly macro taking a template string, declared input/output operands, and optional behavior flags.
Substitute operands by position, index or explicit name; do not accept implicit named arguments; lint unused operands except explicit-register operands and restore assembler state after the block.

Initialize declared input registers from input expressions and transfer declared output registers into their output place expressions after execution; support tied input/output operands and discarded outputs.
Treat an ordinary output as writable at any time and prevent it from sharing a register with other arguments.
Allow a late output to reuse an input register only when all inputs have been read before that output is written.
Accept explicit registers or register classes, enforce aliases/overlap and type/size constraints, and reject repeated conflicting explicit registers or oversized values.
Support constant-expression immediate operands and symbol operands with their stated substitutions.
Apply template modifiers only to operand formatting, not register allocation, with one modifier per placeholder.
Preserve the specified defaults and semantics for side effects, memory access, flags, non-returning blocks and stack use; reject simultaneous nomem and readonly.
Preserve declared clobbers and the specified backend mappings, including prohibiting unwinding from an assembly block.
Initially support the stated ARM, x86 and RISC-V architecture families, including the listed AArch64 cases and register tables.

preferred_conditions.predicate: Use readable operand syntax that can be implemented across backends.
Reduce register pressure through explicit late-output declarations while preserving correctness.
Keep operand constraints simple and defer more complex operand forms.

unnecessary_conditions.predicate: Support memory operands in the initial design.
Implement an embedded assembler-language parser with full instruction-side-effect knowledge.
Support flag-output operands, goto labels, per-instance unique identifiers, or automatic function-call clobber sets in the initial interface.
